newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Slovnaft shares ease pushing SAX to yr-low.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Slovnaft shares ease pushing SAX to yr-low.

text.p: Modest losses to blue chip Slovnaft on Monday pushed the Bratislava Stock Exchange's SAX index down 2.15 points to a year-low of 168.55.
Slovnaft, the most-capitalised issue on the bourse, closed down 32 crowns at 818, with traders predicting a further decline in the share.
"If the current, desperate situation on the bourse continues, I see Slovnaft breaking through the 800-crown level very soon," Bohus Betko of ING Barings said.
"And I have to add I don't see any chance for a change for the better (for the BSE) in the near future," he added.

Several other major issues edged up in very thin trading. Steel maker VSZ eased by two crowns, on a floor volume of 114 shares, while the bank VUB closed up four crowns at 1,500, on a paltry 25 shares.
"Mainly domestic holders are about to sell their stocks pretty soon, as it becomes too expensive for them to keep prices more or less steady," Betko said.
"But I don't expect volumes to increase too much, as general interest in trading remains very low," he added.

Overall, volume fell to 183,180 shares, from 696,634 shares traded on Friday, while turnover decreased to 116.15 million crowns, from 440.57 million. Most of the activity came off market in the form of direct and block trades.
